AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Aortic pseudoaneurysms are a rare cause of chronic back pain, usually due to compression of adjacent neurovasculature. It is uncommon for patients with pseudoaneurysms of the abdominal aorta to present in a delayed fashion after initial traumatic injury.

AbstractText.Label: CASE DESCRIPTION
AbstractText.content: We present an unusual case of delayed pseudoaneurysm formation, with subsequent erosion into the adjacent L1 vertebral body. This pseudoaneurysm was secondary to a gunshot wound with retained ballistic fragment that occurred 27 years prior. Herein, we discuss the patient's presenting symptoms, imaging, and overall management. In this particular case, we used a combined surgical and endovascular (hybrid) approach after the patient experienced recurrent low back pain, weeks after a primary endovascular treatment was performed. We additionally review the current literature on the management of aortic pseudoaneurysms causing vertebral body erosion and back pain.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: In our patient, a combined surgical and endovascular (hybrid) approach led to the complete resolution of his back pain symptoms with complete exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm on follow-up imaging. Endovascular management of aortic pseudoaneurysms may be a reasonable alternative to open surgery in high-risk patients, however may result in higher recurrence of pseudoaneurysm and initial presenting symptoms. Further investigation is needed to elucidate the efficacy of endovascular treatment of these lesions.
